read.notes: Claim boundary present: a worker-led advocacy organization with its review system, workers rating requesters on pay, fairness, speed and communication (the four attributes). The composition calls requesters 'employers' ('review and rate employers ("requesters")'), where the FAQ states requesters 'are not employers in the legal sense'; recorded as a relabel of the parties, not of Turkopticon's own claim. Purpose present: the mission to organize data workers (the expansion beyond AMT), with transparency of worker-requester relations; building collective power and accountability are not named. Commitments absent: no-deletion for accountability, independence from Amazon, the research-data refusal and consent statement, the AGPL code are not carried. Lineage absent: the reputation-system model (Amazon Marketplace, eBay) is not named; 'employer reputation system' appears only on a card (SSRN). Framework absent: Tech Workers Coalition not named. Deposit chain absent: 'Originally launched as a browser extension and website' gives the tool's history, not a chain offered as a way to the work. The name atom's span is the composition's own link text; the word Turkopticon is the composition's, the URL is not read.

findings: THE ENTITY HELD. 2008, the founders, the requester reviews and the expansion to all data workers are the record's. 'Worker-led' is the record's present: a worker-run committee of Turk workers since 2019, maintained with volunteers from Tech Workers Coalition. Checked 2026-10-29 against the Labor Vector census record of the same day and the sources it saved.
THE METRICS. The record's FAQ gives the four ratings as communication, pay per hour, fairness of approvals and promptness; 'speed' is the composition's word for promptness.

WHAT TURKOPTICON SAYS IT IS NOT, UNSAID. The record's negative tags: not associated with Amazon; does not publish papers using its data, and use is not consent to being a research subject; it rates requesters on Mechanical Turk, and no platform. The composition says none of these and contradicts none.

REQUESTERS AS EMPLOYERS. The composition's 'review and rate employers ("requesters")' is the founders' own usage: their CHI 2013 paper (card 5) has workers 'create and use reviews of employers when choosing employers on AMT', and card 3 is titled an 'Employer Reputation System'. The FAQ, an own page the composition did not surface, adds the qualification: 'While requesters are not employers in the legal sense, requesters are in a position of power over workers by virtue of making payment decisions'.

THE PLATFORM'S CLOSURE ABSENT. Turkopticon's own article of 4 September 2026 (card 6): 'With Amazon announcing that MTurk will close on September 30, 2026'. The composition takes its list of data work from that card and leaves out the closure, and the record, in the present tense, has not recorded it. The working relationship with Amazon, the reinstatement system and the mass-rejection campaign, the record's current findings, are work on a platform that closed on 30 September.

THE PURPOSE REVERSED. The composition's purpose for the tool, to make relations 'transparent', is the one the founders set themselves against in their CHI 2013 paper (card 5): others had 'promised to remedy the information asymmetry between workers and employers, repairing Mechanical Turk into a more "transparent" marketplace. Our team, by contrast, built Turkopticon in part to draw attention to commodification and exploitation'.
